question: Which parameter-space quantities are exactly conserved by gradient flow in residual and attention architectures, and how faithfully do discrete stochastic updates preserve them?

key_findings.claim: A residual skip does not create new conservation laws for a block: the complete laws are inherited from the trainable residual branch under the paper's architectural assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: By characterizing infinitesimal parameter transformations that leave the block function unchanged, the authors derive complete conservation-law families for shallow linear and ReLU convolutional blocks and show how the residual addition preserves the branch characterization.

anchors.section: Completeness results for linear/ReLU convolutional branches

key_findings.claim: The single-attention-layer analysis yields explicit balance-type invariants tied to value/output and query/key reparameterization symmetries.
key_findings.evidence: The paper specializes its general loss-invariance framework to attention and derives matrix-valued conserved quantities, while carefully limiting the completeness claim to the modeled attention configuration.

key_findings.claim: Local laws can be established for a subset of parameters even inside a larger network when the associated invariance is confined to that module.
key_findings.evidence: A modular proposition links transformations of selected parameters to conservation under the whole-network gradient flow, enabling blockwise statements without solving all global symmetries.

anchors.section: 2 From subset loss invariance to local conservation

key_findings.claim: Under bounded gradient and Hessian assumptions, SGD violates an exact gradient-flow invariant only at second order in the step size, and the experiments follow that predicted scaling.
key_findings.evidence: A Taylor bound gives cumulative error proportional to the sum of squared learning rates. ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and a transformer on IMDb show conservation-error slopes close to the theoretical quadratic behavior over tested step sizes.

method.core_idea: Derive architecture-specific conservation laws from smooth parameter transformations that leave a module's realized function and hence its loss invariant.
method.mechanism: The authors characterize infinitesimal symmetry directions for residual convolutional and attention blocks, convert their orthogonality to the gradient into conserved scalar or matrix quantities, prove completeness in selected cases, and bound drift introduced by discrete SGD through Taylor expansion.
assumptions: Gradient flow is continuous and the loss and parameterization have the differentiability needed for the symmetry argument.
Completeness results apply to the specified shallow linear/ReLU blocks and simplified attention layer, not every modern implementation detail.
The SGD drift bound assumes bounded gradients and Hessians along the optimization path.
Normalization, nonlinear gates, multi-head coupling, and other omitted components may alter the invariance group.

techniques.role: Finds transformations under which a block computes exactly the same function.
Converts infinitesimal loss invariance into quantities constant along gradient flow.
Transfers a subset-parameter symmetry into an invariant inside a composite network.
Quantifies how discretization changes a continuous-time conservation law.

evaluations.setting: ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10 under several constant learning rates.
evaluations.metric: Relative drift of derived residual-block conservation quantities.
evaluations.result: Measured drift grows approximately quadratically with step size over the tested regime, consistent with the bound.
evaluations.baseline: The zero-drift prediction of exact gradient flow and the theoretical step-size-squared slope.

evaluations.setting: Transformer text classifier trained on IMDb.
evaluations.metric: Evolution of attention conservation error alongside training loss.
evaluations.result: The relevant invariant remains approximately conserved and its discretization error follows the expected learning-rate trend.
evaluations.baseline: Exact conservation in continuous time and multiple discrete step sizes.

evaluations.setting: Symbolic analysis of shallow linear/ReLU convolutional residual branches and a single attention layer.
evaluations.metric: Completeness of the characterized infinitesimal conservation-law space.
evaluations.result: Complete families are established for the paper's specified blocks; broader modern components are outside scope.
evaluations.baseline: Known balance laws for homogeneous feed-forward networks.

limitations: Completeness does not cover full multi-head transformer stacks with normalization, gating, positional transformations, and tied parameters.
The empirical checks test invariance drift, not a demonstrated improvement in optimization or generalization.
The SGD result is an upper-bound scaling under boundedness assumptions and does not model adaptive optimizers or momentum directly.
The analysis emphasizes exact differentiable symmetries and may miss approximate or data-dependent invariants.
failure_modes: Layer normalization, weight decay, momentum, or adaptive preconditioning can explicitly break a derived gradient-flow law.
Large learning rates can leave the local Taylor regime in which quadratic drift is informative.
A symmetry valid for an isolated branch may be destroyed by parameter sharing or cross-module constraints.
Numerically small invariant drift can coexist with poor task learning because conservation is diagnostic, not an objective.
reusable_insights: Architecture symmetries give exact unit tests for optimizers and implementations.
Subset-parameter invariance is a modular route to analyzing otherwise intractable deep networks.
The sum of squared step sizes is a natural budget for accumulated discretization error in gradient-flow invariants.
open_questions: What is the complete conservation structure of practical pre-normalized multi-head transformers with RoPE and gated MLPs?
Can invariant drift predict training instabilities or guide learning-rate schedules?
How do Adam, momentum, weight decay, and quantized updates transform or destroy these laws?

competitive_landscape.title: Conservation Laws for Modern Neural Architectures
competitive_landscape.relationship: Extends conservation-law analysis to a broader set of components including modern activations, rotary position encodings, multi-head attention, and mixture-of-experts structures.
competitive_landscape.difference: It expands architectural coverage beyond the simplified residual and attention blocks treated here; this paper supplies earlier completeness and SGD-drift arguments for those core blocks.

competitive_landscape.title: Unification of Symmetries Inside Neural Networks: Transformer, Feedforward and Neural ODE
competitive_landscape.relationship: Systematizes reparameterization symmetries across transformers and other neural architectures.
competitive_landscape.difference: It centers on symmetry unification and equivalence; the present work derives complete conservation-law families for selected blocks and quantifies their discrete-SGD drift.

competitive_landscape.title: The activity-weight duality in feed forward neural networks: The geometric determinants of generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses parameter and activity geometry to construct scale-aware quantities for feed-forward network optimization and generalization.
competitive_landscape.difference: Activity-weight duality targets Hessian/generalization geometry; this paper derives exact Noether-style invariants from architecture symmetries in residual and attention modules.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The work gives complete conservation laws for specified residual and attention modules and proves controlled approximate conservation under stochastic gradient steps.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It connects explicit module symmetries to laws, proves completeness in tractable cases, and verifies the predicted step-size-squared error on vision and text models.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The modular completeness and discrete-drift bridge are substantive; architectural omissions mean the results should not be read as a complete transformer theory.
